next.name: GOLD LOCUST
next.headline: GOLD LOCUST: the FIN7 and Carbanak cluster, from card thieves to loaders and ransomware links
next.in_short: Secureworks tracks GOLD LOCUST, whose aliases include FIN7 and Carbanak. Reports describe mailed USB drives, phishing loaders, anti-EDR tools and links to ransomware crews. Several links are vendor assessments.

sentences.t: Secureworks tracks this actor as GOLD LOCUST. The catalogue lists the aliases Anunak, Carbanak, Carbon Spider, FIN7 and Silicon.
The catalogue lists Carbanak as the actor's tool.
Morphisec Labs says it has tracked FIN7, which it also calls the Carbanak Group, for several years.
An FBI FLASH alert said FIN7 mailed packages through USPS to businesses in the retail, restaurant and hotel industries.
BleepingComputer reports that in 2018 FIN7 hacked Saks Fifth Avenue and Lord & Taylor to steal payment card information.
In the FBI alert, the mailed USB drives were set up to emulate keystrokes. One package was described as coming from Best Buy, with a gift card as bait.
Morphisec describes a chain that starts with a phishing invoice lure. VBScript stages run in memory, and a final script loads Carbanak reflectively.

Malwarebytes attributes a late-June malspam campaign to FIN7. It dropped JSSLoader, which Malwarebytes calls a rewrite with expanded abilities, including data exfiltration, plus a second payload written in .NET.

Harfanglab says Sentinel Labs links, with high confidence, the sellers of the anti-EDR tool AvNeutralizer to the FIN7 cluster. Harfanglab says the tool relies on vulnerable drivers to kill EDR processes.
Harfanglab adds that the developers of the PackXOR packer might be connected to FIN7. It says the packer appears to be used for activity unrelated to FIN7.
The FBI alert behind the BleepingComputer report was issued in March 2020. It said the USB drives were used to fetch GRIFFON malware.
Morphisec says it intercepted its JSSLoader attack chain in a customer network in December 2020.
In November 2022, SentinelLABS published a report on Black Basta attacks. Its title says the custom EDR evasion tools are tied to the FIN7 threat actor.

IBM X-Force investigated a Carbanak backdoor associated with a Sodinokibi ransomware attack. It concluded that ITG14 is at least one affiliate group of Sodinokibi. IBM says the Carbanak link rests on similarity to ITG14 tools.
Trend Micro's report on Clop describes links between Clop, TA505 and FIN7. It cites news reporting that FIN7 used the POWERTRASH malware.

Rapid7 assesses that the developers of a Java malware family are likely initial access brokers. It says they potentially provided access to Black Basta or FIN7 affiliates. It also cites GData attributing a python RAT to FIN7.
Treat unexpected USB drives and invoice attachments as hostile, and keep endpoint protection locked down against tampering.
